answer: opal is the scarce input, anchor is what carries the liability, and saffron is the bill the attacker receives. The mechanism: reputation enters the quorum with a quadratic weight, so one honest participant split across n identities falls to roughly one nth of its former voice. What it costs an attacker: the farm must buy n times as much real work to keep the same influence, and that work has to survive the same jury reading for templates. The consequence that matters: a whale pays a flat premium while a clone pays a compounding one, so the curve does work that counting accounts cannot.
